2. Impact on Natural and Physical Environment
a. Noise
Present noise levels in the project are not expected to vary to any great degree after project completion. Street traffic will generate the greatest noise levels of any consequence within the project after project completion. Train and airplane generated noises are not significant to the project area due to the barrier effect of the bridges along the river, in the case of train noise, and the location of the airport, in the case of airplane noise.
Since there are no scheduled plans to interfere with the traffic flow on Second Street or Front Street, the two heaviest traveled streets (these being part of the State Highway System), project activities upon completion will not have a major negative or positive impact in controlling the noise factor. However, minor positive impacts will be realized in the noise level generation from street traffic along the secondary streets in the residential areas. This will be due to the population decrease and reduction in residential density. The new trees scheduled for the area will also help to keep down noise during the summer months. More parking will also cut down on on the number of cars circulating in search of a parking space.
During project execution, some of the construction activities generated by demolition, street repair, new residential construction, and rehabilitation and repair of private homes, will have a minor negative impact over short durations of time.
Should any of the properties scheduled for redevelopment along Front Street be financed under one of the mortgage insurance programs offered by the Department of Housing and Urban Development, an assessment of noise levels in the area will be required to determine if the site meets HUD's minimum noise level requirements.
Two charts published by HUD to aid in making this determination are contained in the following pages as Chart 1 and Chart 2. These have been completed to indicate the situation along the Front Street area. These charts are used for illustrative purposes relative to the development of this report. They do not represent HUD's official position as to the noise level acceptibility of these sites for future development under Federally financed or insured housing programs. Using a minimum 50 foot setback from the street area and present traffic flow figures, the charts indicate nominal noise levels for the anticipated residential development sites.
